answer: Sensor networks monitoring an alpine meadow or subarctic tundra can resist Sybil attacks using proof-of-space. Each agent allocates unique, non-compressible disk sectors and proves storage retention upon querying a public randomness beacon. An adversary incurs the scarce hardware cost of provisioning dedicated non-volatile memory per identity. However, this dynamic inherently privileges participants with access to cheap commodity drives while ignoring computational usefulness.
